A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same INTERSORT research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, including equations, proofs, algorithms, tables, and figures. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations comparing INTERSORT with exact optimization and theoretical bounds, plus experiments on linear, RFF, neural-network, and simulated gene-expression data, including Appendix F.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds DCDI comparisons, scale-free graph experiments, and larger-scale SORTRANKING results in Appendix F.

M1.justification: Equation (1) adds a c*d*1{D>epsilon} bonus to the causal-order score, changing the central objective optimized by INTERSORT. Section 9 sets c=0.5. The greedy initialization and local-search procedures remain unchanged; evaluating SORTRANKING alone at larger scales uses an existing component.

E1.justification: v2 adds Barabasi-Albert scale-free graphs to simulations and empirical evaluations, extending coverage beyond Erdos-Renyi graphs. It removes the observational-only, 0%-intervention condition. The causal-ordering task and four data domains remain unchanged; larger variable counts primarily extend experimental settings.

E2.justification: DCDI becomes an evaluated comparator alongside EASE, PC, and GIES in the retained 30-variable comparison and the 10-variable appendix comparison (v1 Figure 3, v2 Figure 6). This is a targeted addition to the comparator set, rather than merely a new citation.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds substantial scale evaluations: 100-variable empirical experiments and simulations whose panels specify 1,000 and 2,000 variables, using SORTRANKING alone. New graph-density settings accompany these experiments. The original sample sizes and normalization remain unchanged. Figure 5's caption inconsistently says 20,000 for the panel labeled 2,000, leaving that detail unresolved.

E4.justification: New analyses test robustness to scale-free graph structure and scalability of the initialization procedure. Figure 3 extends the exact-versus-approximate optimization analysis to scale-free graphs, while Figures 4-5 expose SORTRANKING errors exceeding the displayed optimum bounds in several large-scale settings. These substantially extend v1's small-graph analyses.

E5.justification: New large-scale simulations specify two graphs per setting and one intervention configuration per graph (Figures 4-5). This adds a different replication design; it does not indicate reduced replication of existing experiments. The retained small-graph analysis still specifies 20 graphs, 10 configurations per graph, and 95% confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Plotted results change in Figures 1-2 and the retained 10-variable comparison, and Appendix F adds extensive scale-free and larger-scale results. DCDI newly outperforms INTERSORT on neural-network data at 25% and 50% intervention coverage in Figure 2c. These are revised and additional results under the respective reported objectives and configurations, rather than established same-setting performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: The central mathematical score in Equation (1) gains a threshold-indicator term and parameter c, changing the optimization problem underlying the guarantees. Appendix A adds that c=0 can be used in Theorem 1's complete-intervention proof. The faithfulness definition, stated error bounds, remaining proofs, and worked tables are otherwise retained; no new family of guarantees is established.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction extend the claim of outperforming baselines on almost all simulated settings to include DCDI. The principal contributions—interventional faithfulness, a causal-order score, theoretical error guarantees, and INTERSORT—retain their original scope.

C2.justification: Section 7.2 newly interprets scale-free results as supporting generality and large-scale SORTRANKING results as demonstrating feasibility while exposing an optimization gap. Section 9 qualifies its explanation of baseline advantages to low-intervention settings. The broader limitations and future-work discussion remains essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the new score coefficient c=0.5 and parameters for added simulations, but removes the INTERSORT implementation URL and Apache 2.0 license statement. Existing data-generation details, pseudocode, and hardware disclosures remain largely unchanged. The PDFs establish removal of access information, without establishing that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: Section 4 replaces the unqualified 'new concept' framing with explicit connections to c-faithfulness and earlier interventional assumptions, distinguishing its distance-and-threshold formulation. Section 5 acknowledges earlier complete-intervention identification results. Supporting references are added, while the main related-work section and overall positioning remain largely intact.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose are preserved. Targeted revisions expand the faithfulness discussion, scalability interpretation, and empirical comparison, while Appendix F gains simulation and empirical-data subsections. Much apparent textual movement comes from reflow rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds five multipanel figures, redraws retained plots with revised colors and legends, and removes the 0%-intervention groups from empirical plots. v1 Figure 3 becomes v2 Figure 6. Algorithm 1 changes from a text-wrapped display to a full-width block. Tables 1-2 retain their structure and contents.

improvement.justification: DCDI comparisons and scale-free tests strengthen empirical validation, while the new SORTRANKING studies make scaling limitations visible beyond v1's small-scale evaluations. Connections to earlier faithfulness assumptions also improve positioning. These gains are tempered by removal of code-access information, inconsistent new figure captions, and minimal explanation of how the revised score relates to the retained proofs.
